title: AP Statistics Foundation Pilot Learning Library
description: A text-first, independently authored AP Statistics foundation library with five unit chapters, structured lessons, retrieval checks, study cards, memory aids, and explicitly unscored FRQ-planning workshops. It is not released, official, calibrated, or score-predictive.

blueprint.pilotNote: A 200-item foundation sampler across the five revised Fall 2026 units, with two hundred original single-choice items, native chapters, and unscored planning workshops.

skills.label: Selecting Statistical Methods
skills.description: Select an investigative question and an appropriate statistical method for the data and goal.

skills.label: Analyzing Data
skills.description: Identify, represent, calculate, and compare statistical information needed to answer a question.

skills.label: Using Probability and Simulation
skills.description: Calculate or estimate probabilities, parameters, intervals, and inference results.

skills.label: Statistical Argumentation
skills.description: Describe distributions, interpret results, verify conditions, and justify a claim in context.

constructedResponseWorkshops.title: Study design planning workshop
constructedResponseWorkshops.prompt: Plan a sampling or experimental study for a question about student transportation. Identify the population, observational units, variables, sampling or assignment method, and the conclusion the design could support.
selfCheck: Name the target population and parameter.
Explain how randomization enters the design.
State whether the design supports generalization, causation, or both.
constructedResponseWorkshops.scoreMeaning: No score is produced. This is a planning and self-check resource, not automated FRQ scoring.
constructedResponseWorkshops.reviewNote: Original workshop; independent AP Statistics subject-expert and accessibility review remain pending.

constructedResponseWorkshops.title: Data description planning workshop
constructedResponseWorkshops.prompt: Plan a concise description of a one-variable distribution and a comparison of two groups. Specify the display, center, spread, and unusual features you would report.
selfCheck: Match each display to the variable type.
Use resistant summaries when outliers or skewness matter.
Compare groups using the same units and summaries.
constructedResponseWorkshops.scoreMeaning: No score is produced. This is a planning and self-check resource, not automated FRQ scoring.

constructedResponseWorkshops.title: Proportion inference planning workshop
constructedResponseWorkshops.prompt: Plan a confidence interval or hypothesis test for a population proportion using a public-opinion question. Write the parameter, conditions, method, and contextual interpretation.
selfCheck: Use p for the population proportion.
Check randomization, independence, and large counts.
Interpret the interval or p-value without claiming proof.

constructedResponseWorkshops.title: Means and regression planning workshop
constructedResponseWorkshops.prompt: Plan an inference or regression response about a quantitative outcome. Identify the target, method, assumptions, evidence, and limits of the conclusion.
selfCheck: Use residuals and r-squared as model evidence, not causal proof.
Keep extrapolation and lurking variables visible.
